parity_notes_html: AsOfUtc: discrepancy with the playbook table. Neither OEE proc receives AsOfUtc, and the job adds no cutoff filter. as_of_utc goes only into the imported KAN-8 stage_downtime_local (start_utc < AsOfUtc, open events capped), which feeds stg.downtime_shift_seg → mes.usp_calc_planned_time. An earlier cutoff therefore changes OEE (2025-11-10: 92 values; 2025-11-16 12:00: 9; 2025-11-20: 7; 2025-11-17 00:00:01: 0), and the expected earlier-cutoff outcome is reconcile FAIL. The playbook's AsOfUtc table lists PL_OEE as IDENTICAL, which is wrong for this pipeline.

Ticket behaviour not met, by design. KAN-7 says "planned minutes = shift length minus PLANNED downtime". Legacy computes planned_dt_min but never uses it: planned_min = shift_minutes (DATEDIFF on UTC bounds; 540/780 on fall-back nights), and availability = (shift − unplanned) / shift. The extract agrees: PLT02-L1 2025-10-30 S1 has 90 planned downtime minutes, planned_min=480, availability=1.0000.

Rounding. The extract matches each metric's exact ratio rounded once to 4 dp, half away from zero, with OEE = (s−u)·G / (s·I) and a NULLIF guard on total units. A chain of Spark decimal divisions gives 4 diffs, and multiplying rounded components also differs (PLT03-L1 2025-10-23 S3: 0.8655 vs 0.8654). The job uses exact DECIMAL(38,0) integer arithmetic.
Downtime minutes use DATEDIFF(MINUTE) on local segment bounds via KAN-8's datediff_minute. The hard-coded production_day >= '2025-10-20' filter is kept.

Canonical seed edge cases. PLT06-L4 2025-11-04 (zero-total day) gives NULL quality and oee and performance 0.0000. SKU-XX99 buckets are dropped by the dim.sku inner join. Spring-forward days, boundary straddles, duplicates, unknown keys, open events and pre-floor rows are covered by the unit tests and the fuzz variants.
No seed tuning was needed. The existing seed reproduces the extract byte-for-byte. The seed was not fitted to the snapshot.
Line terminator. MANIFEST shows bcp -r\n, but the committed extract uses CRLF. The byte-compare renders CRLF.
NULLs in NOT NULL source columns (impossible in legacy) are dropped and counted by the imported stages. INT / DECIMAL overflow raises, like SQL Server.
Ambiguous / gap local times follow java.time / zoneinfo fold=0 (the documented AT TIME ZONE behaviour). This was not verified against a live SQL Server.
The ADF JSON in lakehouse/adf/ was reviewed, not deployed. Nothing here ran on ADF or Databricks.
